title: Book One · Chapter 119: The Space by the Gate
story:
Mrs Lan opens the green gate all the way. The gate stops near the wall.

“This must stay clear,” she says.

Mr Qiu stands beside her. Mum has a piece of string. Ronan holds a short stick. He will mark the ground with it.

The rain has stopped for an hour. Water still drops from the roofs. A bird makes a great noise somewhere beyond the yard.

“He likes the idea,” Ronan says.

“He has not seen the price,” Mr Qiu says.

Mrs Lan points to the inside wall, near the gate. There is a dry part under the roof of her front room. A small table could stand there. People could come to it from the street. They would not walk through the yard.

“A table, not a shop,” she says. “I live here.”

“I know.”

“And nothing beside the tap.”

Mum lays the string across the dry space. Ronan holds one end. Mr Qiu bends to look.

“My narrow board would fit.”

“The board has no legs,” Mrs Lan says.

“It has two.”

“Two legs will not hold the table up.”

Mum laughs. Mr Qiu smiles and looks at the ground.

“I can ask about two low stands.”

Dad can make them, Ronan thinks. He opens his mouth. Dad is at work. Dad has not heard any of this.

“We can ask Dad. Is it safe? He can check,” he says instead.

Mrs Lan nods. She steps over the string and walks through the gate. Then Mum does the same with a full washing basket. Mr Qiu moves back to give her room.

“Try it with a chair here,” Mum says.

Ronan brings a small chair from the kitchen. He sets it at the end of the string. The table might come as far as this. Mum comes through again. The basket hits the chair.

“My washing basket cannot get through. It says no,” she says.

They move the string closer to the wall. This time the basket passes. Mrs Lan tries the gate again. It opens all the way.

Ronan makes two little marks with the stick. He looks at the small marks. The stall may fit between them.

“Morning and afternoon?” Mr Qiu asks.

“We will try three days,” Mrs Lan says. “No evening selling. Pack everything away before supper. Then we talk again.”

Mr Qiu looks towards his crates in the front room.

“And the books at night?”

“We need a dry place. My sister needs her bed.”

Mum looks at a high empty shelf in the small side space by the gate.

“Could the boxes go there?”

Mrs Lan thinks. She opens the little side door and checks the roof herself. Then she shuts it.

“Dad must look first. Is the shelf dry? Is the roof good? We need to know.”

Ronan picks up the string. The marks remain on the ground. Now they have a place to try for the table. They still need a table and a dry shelf. Mrs Lan has not agreed to more yet.

He takes the chair back to the kitchen. On the way it catches his coat. He stops and turns the chair. A table will be harder to move. He goes outside again and tells Mr Qiu about the turn by the side door. The old man walks over to look. They decide the small boxes must come through first.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：stay clear＝保持畅通；fit＝放得下；try it＝试一试。

情节提示：string＝细绳；stand＝这里指支架；washing basket＝洗衣篮。

理解：1. 大家为什么拿洗衣篮试走？2. 哪些事情还没有决定？
